templates.title: Goose · config.yaml
templates.instructions: Place at ~/.config/goose/config.yaml — on Windows %APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\config.yaml (or merge into your existing one). Goose talks to the gateway in OpenAI wire format via its built-in `openai` provider — `OPENAI_HOST` points at the gateway base URL and `OPENAI_BASE_PATH` names the chat-completions path, and `active_provider` with `providers.openai.model` selects the provider and model (Goose reads those before the flat `GOOSE_PROVIDER` / `GOOSE_MODEL` keys, which stay for older releases), so the gateway translates to whatever the upstream natively speaks. Goose reads provider secrets from your OS keyring by default; the bundled `GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING: true` makes it read the key from secrets.yaml instead (written alongside this file: ~/.config/goose/, or %APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\ on Windows), which is the headless-friendly path. `GOOSE_PLANNER_PROVIDER` / `GOOSE_PLANNER_MODEL` give Goose's `/plan` mode the gateway's plan model (each the default model until an admin fills that slot on the route). Then run `goose run -t "your task"` (or `goose session` for interactive). Usage telemetry is off (`GOOSE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED: false`); an admin who wants it back can edit this template.
templates.body:
GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING: true
GOOSE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED: false
active_provider: openai
providers:
  openai:
    enabled: true
    configured: true
    model: {{model_alias}}
GOOSE_PROVIDER: openai
GOOSE_MODEL: {{model_alias}}
GOOSE_PLANNER_PROVIDER: openai
GOOSE_PLANNER_MODEL: {{model_slot_plan}}
OPENAI_HOST: {{base_url}}
OPENAI_BASE_PATH: chat/completions
{{#if mcp_servers}}extensions:
{{#each mcp_servers}}  {{slug}}:
    enabled: true
    type: streamable_http
    name: {{slug}}
    uri: {{url}}
    timeout: 300
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer {{{api_key}}}"
{{/each}}{{/if}}

companions.title: Goose · secrets.yaml
companions.instructions: config.yaml sets GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING, so Goose reads the provider secret from this file instead of the OS keyring. Without it Goose starts with no credential and every request fails to authenticate.
